The same burst shape appears on 7 other customers' cards (C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C03633-K1, C05851-K1) in the prior 30 days, so it is coordinated rather than card testing (no small probes) or a known category. sar.narrative: Between 2016-11-29 19:00 and 2016-11-29 19:36, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,922.43 were made on card(s) C12641-K2 belonging to customer C12641. The activity comprised 4 online transaction(s) under product code(s) C, in billing region 143, 436. Online transactions came from device profile(s) Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1440x900; SM-G930V Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome generic for android | 1920x1080. The purchases were placed within minutes of each other, each just below a $500 threshold, a pattern that avoids single-transaction limits. When contacted: Customer states they did not make the $484.48 transaction and still has the card (simulated). The same burst shape was found on 8 cards of 8 different customers in the preceding 30 days, indicating coordinated abuse (policy R9). The amount exceeds the $1,000 reporting threshold. Total suspicious amount: $1,922.43. Actions recommended: BLOCK_CARD, CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST.
